title: React & Frontend Follow-ups
description: Deep-dive into React internals, performance debugging, state architecture, and Next.js patterns. Each lesson is framed as a realistic senior-engineer interview follow-up with actionable reasoning and code examples.

data.text: These eight lessons cover the follow-up questions a senior React engineer is likely to face after the initial system design round. Interviewers use them to test depth: can you debug a performance problem from first principles, or do you reach for useMemo reflexively? Can you distinguish server state from client state, or do you put everything in Redux?

data.title: Study strategy
items: Start with the re-rendering lesson — it is the foundation for most React performance discussions.
Move to state architecture (React Query vs Redux) to show you understand data flow.
Study memory leaks and bundle size to demonstrate tooling fluency.
Finish with hydration, Server Components, and optimistic updates for full-stack depth.

data.title: Interview tip
data.text: For each follow-up, start by asking the interviewer for specifics: 'What does the component do? How many users see it? What have you tried so far?' A senior engineer gathers context before proposing solutions.

whatYouLearn: Diagnose unnecessary React re-renders using Profiler, why-did-you-render, and component boundaries
Decide between React Query and Redux for server vs client state
Identify and fix React memory leaks with Chrome DevTools and heap snapshots
Apply bundle-splitting strategies to reduce initial JavaScript payload
Understand hydration mismatch causes and SSR/CSR divergence patterns
Choose between Server and Client Components in Next.js App Router
Implement optimistic UI updates with rollback and error recovery
Debug poor Interaction to Next Paint (INP) using Chrome Performance tools
